description:
DECISION: In parse_rnews_batch_plain(), the byte count parsed from each '#! rnews N' header is checked against MAX_RNEWS_ARTICLE_BYTES before any slice indexing, and the end-of-article position is computed with checked_add() rather than unchecked addition.

WHY RIGHT: An attacker controls the byte count field in the header. Without the range check, a count of usize::MAX - pos would wrap or panic in debug mode when used as a slice index. The explicit MAX_RNEWS_ARTICLE_BYTES check before the slice means the article is rejected with a typed MalformedBatch error rather than a panic or silent truncation. The checked_add() handles the residual case where pos + count would overflow even after the per-article cap (e.g. two near-max articles near the end of a large batch). Both defences are needed: the per-article cap prevents any single item from being too large; the overflow check prevents the cumulative position from wrapping.

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED:
- Saturating addition: would silently cap the position and mismatch the declared length, producing a confusing truncation error rather than a clear overflow error.
- Panic on overflow (default in debug): unacceptable for a network-facing parser; panics are treated as crashes by UUCP batch processors.
title: Per-article byte count range-checked before slice, using checked_add
